threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can always spot a newcomer by how they still try to hail a cab instead of just ordering an Uber. Classic rookie mistake.
Saw a couple arguing over who gets the last of the chicken shop's salt. They ended up sharing it, but the bus driver looked like he wished he could mute them.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a bus at 2 AM with a guy singing opera. The driver just nodded along. That's when I knew this place has a rhythm all its own.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find spontaneous open-air karaoke in the streets on a Saturday night, complete with a crowd of cheering strangers.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows that the best burritos come from the hole-in-the-wall spots, not the trendy chains, especially after a late-night BART delay.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo hop off the 19 and start directing traffic like a conductor. Only in the Tenderloin does Muni turn into a performance art.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's vibrant squares are just for selfies, but they're actually filled with locals sipping café and catching up on gossip.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered looks at El Corte Inglés prices – local shoppers have mastered the art of the discounts and sales.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still use the word 'tube' to refer to public transport. Everyone here calls it 'the Overground' or just 'the train' now.
Last week on the 36, a guy argued with a pigeon over a seat. The pigeon won, strutting around like it owned the bus. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy busking with a parrot on his shoulder outside Reuterstraße, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab stand open at 4 AM serving fresh döner to clubbers, while the U-Bahn is still on strike.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals rush to the bodega for a michelada when they hear the BART alarm. It's like, the only band-aid for a broken commute.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a whiff of burnt rubber on the Civic Center platform today. Turns out, it was just another dog munching on snacks left behind. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that the best vermut spots aren’t on the main streets—they’re tucked away in small plazas, where locals sip slowly and chat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the 5-minute wait for the next tram at Plaça de la Vila; locals know it’s just how it is.
